lines.t: Post came up with the ash cart. Letter for you — from Larkhollow. Smells of varnish and kettle.
"A wild young one of Cass's line has been hanging round the fosterage. Won't let anyone near it. Not even me, and I have biscuits."
"Bring your {starter} and the {leftover} home to the green stone, {player}. I think the three of them want to be in the same chord."
A parcel from Galewick? For me? …New tongs. Proper ones. Someone in that market remembers I used to be a smith.
Take this reply back with you. Tell them the old horseshoe hand's doing fine. Fewer burns these days.
Used to forge horseshoes. Now I mend kin. Better job. Fewer burns.
Rest your troupe? Open the Fosterage ledger? Or are you just warming your hands?

options.label: Help a kin recall a move

lines.t: Salves, cures, a very good burn cream. Everything up here is fireproof except the prices.
Bastian's still grinning. You must've bent without breaking. He likes that more than winning.
Vent's cool, door's open. Bastian's inside. He'll tell you heat is honest. He always does.
Vent's overheated. A water kin could cool it — or wait, I'll open the side sluice for you. Give me a moment.
Hall's shut till the vent's sorted, and the vent's shut till I've a reason. Bastian's orders: 'Nobody sweats in my hall uninvited.'
The stones are loud again. Funny — I don't mind it. Loud's how you know they're still there.
Somebody left flowers at the plaque last week. Mountain lilies. Only one person I know climbs this far with lilies.
"For the herd of the Ash Flats, who ran toward the loudest stone."
I carved that. Took me a whole winter. The stone on the Flats sang so hard that morning the ground shook, and the herd bolted the wrong way.
There was a Chordwright's girl up here that day. Saw all of it. I never saw anyone go so quiet, so young.
Mind the lava. It's railed, but it's still lava.
Every lava channel on Cindral has a rail. Every rail on Cindral is mine. You are welcome.
Don't lean on them after noon, though. Or sit on them. Or lick them. You'd be amazed.
For the herd of the Ash Flats, who ran toward the loudest stone.
Vent's overheated. A water kin could cool it — or wait, I'll open the side sluice for you. Give me a moment.
